skill.name: azure-speech-to-text-rest-py
skill.description: Transcribe short WAV or OGG audio with Azure Speech to Text REST endpoints using synchronous, chunked, or asynchronous Python requests.
skill.summary: Build Python transcription workflows for audio up to 60 seconds without the Azure Speech SDK.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown syntax, official Azure URLs, or expected environment-based credential handling. The skill performs real external audio transmission, and unchecked region values can redirect credential-bearing requests to an unintended host.

remediation.issue: Region values are inserted into credential-bearing request URLs without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only documented Azure region identifiers and verify the final hostname before attaching subscription keys or bearer tokens.

remediation.issue: Audio content is transmitted to Azure Speech endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Obtain user authorization and disclose applicable Azure data handling requirements before uploading sensitive recordings.

remediation.issue: Example HTTP requests omit explicit connection and read timeouts.
remediation.suggestion: Set bounded timeouts and handle timeout exceptions in synchronous, chunked, token, and asynchronous examples.

content.user_title: Transcribe Short Audio with Azure REST
content.value_statement: Short audio transcription often requires unnecessary SDK setup. This skill provides focused Python patterns for calling Azure Speech REST endpoints directly.
actual_capabilities: Creates synchronous Python requests for Azure Speech transcription.
Configures WAV PCM and OGG OPUS content headers.
Streams audio through chunked transfer for lower latency.
Supports subscription key and short-lived bearer token authentication.
Handles recognition statuses and common HTTP errors.
Provides an asynchronous aiohttp transcription pattern.
limitations: The short-audio REST endpoint accepts recordings up to 60 seconds.
Responses contain final results only, without interim transcription.
The workflow does not cover translation, custom models, or batch transcription.
The examples require an Azure Speech resource, valid credentials, and compatible audio.

use_cases.title: Prototype Voice Features
use_cases.description: Add short command or note transcription to a Python prototype without installing the Speech SDK.

use_cases.title: Automate Short Recording Intake
use_cases.description: Transcribe brief WAV or OGG submissions through a lightweight service workflow.

use_cases.title: Compare Recognition Candidates
use_cases.description: Request detailed results and inspect confidence-ranked alternatives for short recordings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Transcriber
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Python function that transcribes [audio path] in [language] with Azure Speech REST. Use environment variables for credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an Audio Format
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the transcription request for [WAV PCM or OGG OPUS]. Explain the required content type and validate the duration limit.

prompt_templates.title: Add Production Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve the transcription workflow with timeouts, recognition status handling, safe error messages, and bounded retries for transient failures.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Async Token Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an aiohttp transcription client using cached bearer tokens, validated Azure regions, chunked input, and concurrent request limits.

output_examples.input: Transcribe a 20-second English WAV recording and return the best text.
output_examples.output: Recognition succeeded. Best transcription: Remind me to buy five pencils.

output_examples.input: Explain why a 90-second recording fails with this endpoint.
output: The short-audio endpoint supports recordings up to 60 seconds.
Use the Speech SDK or Batch Transcription API for longer audio.

output_examples.input: Prepare a detailed French transcription request with safe credential handling.
output: Language is set to fr-FR and detailed results are requested.
The subscription key is loaded from the environment.
The Azure region must be validated before building the endpoint.

best_practices: Use WAV PCM at 16 kHz mono when broad compatibility is required.
Validate the region and language before constructing the request.
Set explicit timeouts and handle every recognition status in production.
anti_patterns: Do not embed subscription keys in source files or prompts.
Do not send recordings longer than 60 seconds to the short-audio endpoint.
Do not log authorization headers, bearer tokens, or sensitive audio content.

faq.question: Does this skill require the Azure Speech SDK?
faq.answer: No. It uses direct HTTPS requests with Python requests or aiohttp.

faq.question: Which audio formats are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover WAV PCM at 16 kHz mono and OGG with OPUS.

faq.question: What is the maximum recording length?
faq.answer: The short-audio endpoint supports recordings up to 60 seconds.

faq.question: Can it return confidence scores?
faq.answer: Yes. Request the detailed response format to receive ranked candidates and confidence values.

faq.question: How should credentials be stored?
faq.answer: Store the subscription key in an environment variable or approved secret manager. Never place it directly in source code.

faq.question: When should another Azure interface be used?
faq.answer: Use the Speech SDK or Batch Transcription API for streaming, interim results, custom models, translation, or longer audio.
